scope: Explicit flat route declarations and the implemented behaviors below. Full Casdoor behavioral equivalence requires additional scenario and deployment acceptance.

items.scope: Existing multipart upload accepts entryId and an explicitly tenant-bound Local provider, persists the object/resource relationship, and previews at most 2 MiB. Local roots are operator-bounded. S3 transcript previews remain outside this implementation.
Reports the running version, operator-pinned release manifest and durable upgrade state. Unconfigured deployments report disabled capabilities.

Validates pinned manifest and package SHA-256/size/platform, records a durable file journal, compensates failures and confirms installed only from a matching running image at startup. Requires operator-supplied installation and restart configuration.
Performs bounded HTTP fingerprint scans, persists results and reports complex CVE rules as unassessed.
Global-admin-only bounded private IPv4 MCP discovery and transactional idempotent Server synchronization.
Uses saved tenant-authorized Server configuration, negotiates Streamable HTTP sessions, JSON/SSE responses and pagination, and preserves existing tool permissions on refresh or failure.
Consumes a separate high-entropy cancellation proof against persistent device state.
Completes an issued device grant once after checking the application, account and approving session.

Uses an application-permitted HTTP/Generic ID verification provider, stores a successful verification audit digest, and revokes verification when identity fields change. Vendor-specific signing adapters remain unimplemented.

additional_security: WebAuthn registration/sign-in use PostgreSQL single-use challenges and native browser credentials, with configured RP/Origin and enforced additional MFA.
Local file operations use an operator-controlled root and exact-owner SHA-256 namespace for tenant callers.
MCP and file S3 requests use checked/pinned DNS addresses, reject private destinations for tenant callers, and disable redirects and environment proxies.

Profile changes persisted through the authenticated API
Cancelling a native WebAuthn request leaves no enrolled credential and permits retry
Native navigator.credentials.create attestation verified and persisted by PostgreSQL

Device browser approval, real OAuth token issuance, single-use completion and cancellation persisted
Passkey sign-in through the UI enforces enrolled MFA before issuing a browser session
Credential deletion persisted and refreshed the browser list
TOTP enrollment, failed proof rejection and password MFA login completed in the browser
Password recovery delivered through a local HTTP email provider and new password login succeeded

validation.counting_note: lib and main each execute the same 37 unit tests. Executions are not distinct business scenarios. The 81 PostgreSQL scenarios are explicitly enabled ignored tests.
